title: MAS-ProVe: Understanding the Process Verification of Multi-Agent Systems
review_status: full-text audit complete; verifier classes, candidate selection, six MAS frameworks, benchmark sizes, repetitions, task-specific improvements and reversals, solvability boundary, and setup adaptations checked
sections_checked: Section 3: N=3 candidate generation and greedy verifier selection
Sections 4.1-4.4 and Tables 1-5: verifier, granularity, context, results and solvability

venue_year_verified: arXiv:2602.03053v2; arXiv record lists ICML 2026 Regular; first submitted 2026-02-03, revised 2026-08-31
evidence_note: The study compares judge, RM and PRM verification at agent-call and iteration levels across six MAS frameworks. Results are non-monotonic and architecture/task dependent; 24/36 configurations favor judge over reward-based verifiers. AIME24/AIME25 each contain 30 questions, GAIA information extraction 103; main tables average three runs. Best verification rarely rescues baseline-unsolvable queries. GAIA receives substantial tool/prompt/operator adaptation, limiting direct cross-task comparability.

evidence_note: EIG reports automatic score 7.41 vs strongest baseline 6.95 on its normalized scale, and blinded overall quality 4.01 vs 3.50 on 24 held-out groups. Confidence intervals exclude zero for overall quality and average rank, but not novelty, feasibility, or context adherence. Controller training uses heuristic preference labels; evaluation is ideation-only and does not establish implementation success.

evidence_note: Under neutral source names and a shared Qwen3-Max evidence pool, LatticeMind reports 0.97 accuracy on 75 ConflictBank examples (73/75) vs 0.61 majority vote. The checker/reconciler ablation uses 50 examples. The four planning benchmarks have n=10-15, include a TravelPlanner regression and a REALM JSSP tie; the repo bridge replays two trajectories. TANGLE (2608.13921) is logged as an abstract-level irreducible-conflict scope counterpoint only, not a full-text audit.
